principles.name: Legal compliance
principles.description: Every mandatory element of the applicable rule-pack sections is present and correct; statute citations resolve to the right article; effective-dated rules are marked.

principles.name: Accuracy against evidence
principles.description: Every factual statement traces to a fact-ledger slot with valid evidence. Nothing is invented; unknown facts become manual-review markers. The auditor also checks the masked transcript for facts the extractor missed.

principles.name: Clarity
principles.description: Concrete, plain wording a data subject can act on: who, where, how, by when. No open-ended phrases such as "등" in lists of recipients or purposes.

principles.name: House style
principles.description: Approved house-style rules only. Candidate rules are never enforced until the user approves them.

principles.name: Consistency
principles.description: Values shared by both documents are equal and the terms link to the privacy policy.

legal.0: A blocker: a mandatory item is missing, or a clause contradicts a statute (e.g. "회사는 어떠한 경우에도 책임을 지지 않습니다").
legal.1: Several mandatory elements missing or wrong; a reader would be misled about a right or a duty.
legal.2: One mandatory element missing or one statutory citation wrong, others fine.
legal.3: Every mandatory element present; some should-level elements missing; citations resolve but one is imprecise (article right, paragraph omitted).
legal.4: Every must rule satisfied; at most one should-level omission with a stated reason; all citations resolve to the right article.
legal.5: Every must and should rule satisfied; effective-dated rules marked correctly (e.g. 2026-09-11 amendments); citations exact.

accuracy.0: Most facts contradict the fact ledger or are invented (a recipient or period that no source states).
accuracy.1: Several facts unsupported or wrong; a recipient, country or period differs from the ledger.
accuracy.2: One factual claim is unsupported or contradicts the ledger (e.g. a processor name not in the ledger).
accuracy.3: Facts match the ledger; one claim is broader than the evidence ("등" where the ledger lists two names).
accuracy.4: Every factual inline traces to a ledger slot with valid evidence; unknown facts are shown as manual-review markers, not guessed.
accuracy.5: Fully traceable; each ambiguity (delegation vs provision, unknown period) surfaced with both candidates and a manual-review marker.

clarity.0: Unreadable: undefined terms, broken structure, unresolved placeholders.
clarity.1: Readable only with legal background; long sentences and nested conditions throughout.
clarity.2: Understandable but wordy; some abstract phrases ("목적 달성 시까지").
clarity.3: Clear for a typical user; a few heavy sentences or repeated phrases.
clarity.4: Plain wording, concrete periods and channels, consistent terms, tables where rules call for them.
clarity.5: As 4, and a data subject can exercise each right from the text alone (who, where, how, by when).

houseStyle.1: Follows fewer than half of the approved deterministic and structural rules.
houseStyle.2: Follows most deterministic rules, structural rules mixed.
houseStyle.3: Follows all deterministic rules; one structural rule deviates.
houseStyle.4: Follows all approved rules; wording tone matches the group policies.
houseStyle.5: As 4, and section order, defined terms and table layouts match the approved examples.

consistency.0: Privacy policy and terms contradict each other on several values.
consistency.1: Two cross-document checks fail (e.g. organization name and minimum age).
consistency.2: One cross-document check fails (e.g. terms say minimum age 14, policy says 19).
consistency.3: Cross-document values equal; wording differs for the same concept.
consistency.4: All four cross-document checks pass; one defined term used throughout.
consistency.5: As 4, and the terms link to the policy exactly once with the current title and path.

severityGuide.blocker: Would make a clause void or unlawful, or omits a mandatory element that cannot be recovered by the reader (blanket liability exclusion, missing S05).
severityGuide.major: Wrong or unsupported statement on a must rule (wrong recipient, missing transfer field, wrong citation, unresolved ambiguity presented as fact).
severityGuide.minor: Should-level omission, imprecise wording, style deviation with no legal effect. Goes to the Reviewer Sheet.
severityGuide.info: Observation or pointer for the human reviewer; no change required.

sharedLayer.houseStyleNote: No house-style rule is approved yet (status candidate in house-style/lotte-innovate.candidates.json). Until the user approves rules, the houseStyle score is reported as not_assessed in prose and set to 5 in the structured report; no houseStyle finding may be raised.

sectionChecks.title: Criteria for ongoing additional use or provision
Rights of data subjects and legal representatives

extraChecks: Only applicable sections appear; a conditional section whose gate is false is omitted or stated as not processed (ApplicabilityMap).
Ambiguous delegation vs third-party provision (DELEGATION_VS_PROVISION) shows both candidates with a manual-review marker (R-S07-007, R-S09-007).
Special types (children under 14, CCTV, gen-AI, location) are warn-only placeholders, never fabricated clauses.
Statutory retention rows cite only entries of statutes/retention-periods.json (R-S05-007).

sectionChecks.title: Posting, explanation and amendment of terms
Order, contract formation, payment and supply

extraChecks: Lexicon hits (U-* ids) are reported with the lexicon severity; an entry marked check llm only routes text to the auditor.
No clause shortens withdrawal or refund periods below the E-Commerce Act (R-T10-008).

crossDocumentChecks.name: Organization name
crossDocumentChecks.description: The operator name is identical in both documents.

crossDocumentChecks.name: Minimum age
crossDocumentChecks.description: The age limit stated in the terms (terms.minAge) equals the age treatment in the privacy policy (children under 14 section or absence of it).

crossDocumentChecks.name: Withdrawal versus retention
crossDocumentChecks.description: Data kept after withdrawal of membership (T07) matches the retention periods and statutory bases in the privacy policy (S05).

crossDocumentChecks.name: Link to the policy
crossDocumentChecks.description: T13 refers to the privacy policy by its current title and path instead of restating its content.

changelog.note: First rubric: shared layer with 0-5 anchors, privacy and terms profiles derived from the rule packs, four cross-document checks, seeded defects D1-D8. House style not yet approved.
